content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Boxoffice Movie Scenes's PostBoxoffice Movie Scenes Verified account6d · Shared with PublicVal Kilmer, one of the stars of "Top Gun", passed away in 2025 after battling throat cancer. Now, he appears once again in the new film "As Deep as the Grave", leaving many viewers wondering how this was even possible.He was originally cast as Father Fintan, a Catholic priest and Native American spiritualist, but was too ill to film his scenes. With the support of Kilmer’s estate and his daughter Mercedes, the filmmakers used generative AI to bring him to life in the movie. The trailer features Kilmer at different ages, sometimes as a ghostly figure, sometimes as a charismatic young priest. In one moving scene, he tells a child, “Don’t fear the dead and don’t fear me,” looking her in the eyes.Director Coerte Voorhees shared, “It was very much designed around him. It drew on his Native American heritage and his ties to and love of the Southwest…His family kept saying how important they thought the movie was and that Val really wanted to be a part of this.”Would you watch a film that uses AI to honor an actor’s legacy? #CuriositiesAll reactions:41087 comments22 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Mike WhittakerIf they gonna bring anyone back in AI form……Barf from Spaceballs please!!!Love ya John Candy! 5d10Rick Freese If his family and estate approved the project, so be it. End of discussion. The main argument against AI depiction is the rights of the artist being depicted. If the artist, their estate or next of kin are happy with it and have a mutual agreement that is satisfactory to both sides, get to it.
